pilot.c1SampleFinding: C1 = vacant lots. A random 10-row sample of C1 accounts returned unambiguous platted-subdivision legal descriptions with real situs addresses: 'La Condesa Subdivision, BLOCK B, LOT 69, ACRES 0.643', 'West Bastrop Village Phase 1, Section 3, BLK B, LOT 25', 'Hacienda Sonoma Subdivision, BLOCK D, LOT 52'. These are ordinary buildable residential lots, not easements or severed interests.
pilot.vintageEvidence: cad_property (Bastrop) has two source vintages: DATA-EXPORT-01.14.2026.zip (ingested 2026-07-14) and stratmap25-landparcels_48021 (the CAD-adjacent stratmap roll, ingested 2026-08-25) -- the TAX ROLL data itself is dated January 2026. txgio_parcel's geometry source is stratmap25-landparcels_48021_bastrop_202503 -- March 2025. This is a 10-month gap between the tax roll's effective date and the GIS parcel fabric's snapshot date, directly consistent with the C1 finding: lots in actively-selling new subdivisions (La Condesa, Hacienda Sonoma, West Bastrop Village) platted or recorded after March 2025 would be on the January 2026 tax roll but absent from the March 2025 GIS pull.

undividedInterestDiscovery.what: 158 of 1,037 accounts (15.2%) carry 'Undivided Interest N%' in their legal_description -- a CAD tax-roll pattern where ONE physical tract is taxed to MULTIPLE co-owners as SEPARATE accounts, each holding a fractional share.
undividedInterestDiscovery.concreteProof: Abstract A119 (Eli Brazlin survey, 156 acres) has 18 separate cad_property accounts, one per co-owner (Becker family members, Koppelman family, Knowles family, trusts, etc.), each with its own prop_id and a distinct Undivided Interest percentage. Direct cross-reference found prop_id 141269 (TENISON, ELIZABETH ANN, same tract, same 156 acres) HAS a real txgio_parcel row (situs 'CR 142', owner name matching). The other 17 accounts for the SAME physical land correctly have no geometry of their own -- they never will, because they are not distinct parcels.
undividedInterestDiscovery.scaleCheck: Grouping all 158 undivided-interest orphan accounts by a normalized tract key (legal_description with the 'Undivided Interest...' suffix stripped) found only 59 DISTINCT underlying tracts. Checking each of the 59 tracts for ANY sibling account (orphan or not) carrying txgio geometry found exactly 1 of 59 covered (the A119 Brazlin case sampled above). The other 58 tracts have NO account with geometry -- genuinely missing, same as the C1 population, just represented by multiple CAD accounts per physical parcel instead of one.

otherSingleOwnerNonC1.topCodes: D1 75 (median 37.8 acres), C3 52 (median 0.23 acres), A1 14 (median 0.40 acres) -- same vintage-gap mechanism plausible for all (one shared cad_property vintage), not separately verified per sub-code given time budget

mechanismStated: Primary: a txgio GIS vintage gap. Bastrop's parcel fabric (stratmap25, March 2025) is 10 months stale relative to the CAD tax roll (January 2026 export) it is supposed to key against. Parcels platted, subdivided, or newly recorded in that 10-month window are real, distinct parcels with real acreage and (72% of the time) a situs address, but have no txgio feature yet. Secondary: an undivided-interest fan-out where CAD represents one physical tract as multiple co-owner accounts; this does not add real distinct-parcel gaps beyond the 59 tracts it touches, but it does mean the raw 1,037-account count overstates the true distinct-parcel gap.
rejectedAlternative: These are inherently non-spatial account types (easements, severed mineral interests, business personal property) that will never have geometry, the same mechanism already characterized for Bastrop's OTHER $0-improvement orphans in R1-crosswalk (~5,416 of the 6,158 total). REJECTED for this specific 1,037-account subset: that population was defined precisely to EXCLUDE it (this card's query requires land_acres>0 AND land_value>0, which the non-spatial personal-property/mineral accounts characteristically lack -- they showed null land_value and null land_acres in R1-crosswalk's own sample). The C1 sample's clean subdivision-lot legal descriptions and situs addresses further rule this out directly: these are ordinary buildable residential/commercial lots, not easements.
